materials.title: Simple Past — regular -ed and key irregular verbs
contentText:
To talk about finished actions in the past, we use the Simple Past. For most verbs, add -ed to the end: play → played, watch → watched, clean → cleaned. Some very common verbs are irregular — they change completely and you need to learn them: go → went, be → was / were, have → had, do → did.

Important: In German, you often say "Ich habe gespielt" (Perfekt) when talking about the past. In English, we say "I played" — no extra helping verb needed. This is the Simple Past.

For negatives, use "did not" (short form: didn't) + the base verb: "I didn't go to school." For questions, use "Did" at the start: "Did you watch TV?" — and use the base verb, not the past form.
I didn't go to school yesterday.

materials.title: Simple Past — gap-fill with word bank
contentText: Yesterday I ___ football in the garden. I was very ___.
Last night, Tom ___ a scary film. He was ___.
This morning, Lisa was very ___. She got up at 6 o'clock.
We ___ to the park after school. It was great!

materials.title: Simple Past — choose the correct form
contentText: Yesterday, I ___ to school. I was ill.
We ___ pizza for dinner last night.
My sister ___ very excited. She ___ a birthday party.

materials.title: Simple Past — find and fix the mistake
contentText: Yesterday I go to the cinema with my friends.
Yesterday I went to the cinema with my friends.
I was very boring at home.
I was very bored at home.
She don't go to school yesterday.
She didn't go to school yesterday.
